newsitem.title: INDIA: India oil well fire rages, American experts on way.
newsitem.headline: India oil well fire rages, American experts on way.

text.p: Firefighters struggled on Thursday to contain a raging blaze caused by a blow-out at an oil and gas exploration well in south-east India, an official of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) said.
A 10-strong American oil firefighting team was expected to arrive in the next two days to tackle the flaming well, Andhra Pradesh state Revenue Minister T.Devender Goud said.

There were no casualties but the blow-out on Wednesday destroyed a 120 million rupee rig and caused around 70 million rupees of damage to other equipment on the well site in the Krishna-Godavari basin.
If the well collapses it could kill the fire, currently shooting 40-metre high blow-torch flames, otherwise the fire firefighters could face a lengthy struggle.
ONGC chairman P.C. Bora, according to Press Trust of India news agency, said it could take 15-20 days to put out the fire.
But a local manager was less optimistic about chances of quelling the fire quickly.
M. Rangarajan, general manager in the Krishna-Godavari basin, said "it will take at least 60 days to extinguish the blow-out from the rogue well."
An official in the ONGC control room at Rajahmundry, 40 km from the Mandapeta West gas well, near Deverapalli on the Andhra coast, said water spraying has started at the site.
"The fire is confined to the cellar pit, and the flames are aound 40 metres high," he said.
Besides the billowing smoke, the light and heat generated by the fire is unbearable. The site is unapproachable upto a 300-metre radius of the inferno.
But the other six exploration wells in the project were working normally, the control room official said.
According to ONGC sources, the blow-out occurred when drilling of the well was in full swing at a depth of 2,754 metres. The well was planned to reach a depth of 4,400 metres.
